newsitem.title: CHINA: SOCCER-CHINA PUTS PLAYERS THROUGH TOUGH WINTER TRAINING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHINA PUTS PLAYERS THROUGH TOUGH WINTER TRAINING.

text.p: China's top soccer league is putting all its players through tough winter training at altitude in a bid to raise the standard of the national game.
All the players from the 12 first division teams, including the full national side, have been in a closed training camp since December, officials said.
They run 10 to 12 kms a day and follow strict exercise routines at the camp in Haigeng, south-western Kunming, at an altitude of nearly 2,000 metres.
Visitors are kept away, the players are not allowed to use mobile telephones and they were banned from going home for the Chinese new year, a local soccer official told Reuters.

"The winter drill this year is a merciless fight against evil habits of not being strict that have long existed on the football field," the Xinhua news agency quoted Wang Junsheng, vice chairman of the China Football Association (CFA), as saying.
The 1996 season was a difficult one for Chinese soccer. Critics said the quality of the league was deteriorating, with less exciting play, fewer goals and more bookings.
The year ended with China losing in the quarter-finals of the Asian Soccer Cup in the United Arab Emirates.
Chinese soccer fans were disappointed with the poor performance of players and believed that most were not physically strong enough to play a full game at high speed, state media said.
